To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The OOT of C → sdG →  sL → S in ABC triblock copolymer thin film induced by solvent vapor is studied.
the morphology transition of SBV thin film induced in the benzene vapor showing the weak selectivity for the polystyrene (PS) block is studied.
the order-order transition of C → sdG → sL → S was induced by the solvent vapor in the thin film of ABC triblock copolymer, and the mechanism is analyzed from total surface area of blocks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the OOT in ABC triblock thin films induced by solvent vapor.
the OOT in the sequence of C, sdG, sL and S, which has not been reported before.
the OOT of the SBV thin film in benzene vapor, which provides a new way to study the phase transitions of ABC triblock copolymer thin film.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OOT in the sequence of C → sdG → sL → S is induced by the solvent vapor in the film.
, for a given solvent, the OOT in SBV thin film is determined by the surface energy of the blocks, the solvent selectivity and the film thickness.
the OOTs are induced in the order of C →  sdG(111)  →  sL(110) and C → sG(111) and sL → s(111).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solvent vapor-induced OOT of ABC triblock copolymer thin film can be understood by the total surface area change in the blocks.
the morphology transition in the film is determined by the competition between the surface area of the core and shell block.
the morphology transition is driven by the minimization of the free energy of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OOT in the film can be induced by the selective solvent, and the sequence of OOT is controlled by the surface free energy of the block copolymer.
the OOTs in ABC triblock copolymer thin films can be induced by a weak solvent vapor, and that the OOT sequence depends on the film thickness.
, in addition to the surface energy, the total surface area is a key factor for the phase selection in ABC triblock copolymers.
